NOTE
    The designation is a declared label of this capture; the probe output above is
    observed fact. The two agree here, so there is no discrepancy to disclose. Had
    they disagreed, the disagreement would be stated plainly rather than reconciled:
    a declared label must never read as though it were captured output, and captured
    output must never read as though it validated the label.

================================================================================
SUBSTITUTIONS APPLIED TO THIS CAPTURE

MAVEN HOME PATH       replaced with <path elided> in PROBE 2. The value was an
                      absolute filesystem path; the version and vendor values on the
                      surrounding lines are behaviour-bearing and are preserved
                      verbatim, so only the path is replaced.
JAVA RUNTIME PATH     replaced with <path elided> at the end of the PROBE 2 Java
                      version line, for the same reason.
CAPTURE DIRECTORY     normalised to <CAPTURE-DIR> by the producer wherever it, the
                      repository root, the home directory or the scratch directory
                      appeared, so the capture does not depend on where it was taken.
CREDENTIAL            never recorded. The producer requires a credential to run and
                      substitutes it out of every byte it writes; the run posture
                      records only its source and the fact that its value is never
                      written. No credential, keystore or trust-store value appears.
MODULE ACCESS ARG     none present, therefore none replaced. No captured value here
                      contained a module-access JVM argument.
NOTHING ELSE          no other value was altered. Every substitution above is applied
                      inside the producing pipeline, never by hand after the fact: a
                      hand-edited capture is not evidence.

================================================================================
GOVERNING RULES AND PROVENANCE

RULES DOCUMENT        none on disk
RULES IN FORCE        14 (7 core, 7 transformation)
IDENTIFIER SCHEME     R-1..R-7 and R-T1..R-T7 are the migration plan's own
                      navigational convention, not quoted rule titles.

Both provenance facts are stated together, because either one alone misleads.
There is no on-disk user rules document for this project: the rules facility was
queried and returned "No user rules provided." on every call, and that read was
complete rather than partial. Rules are nonetheless present and binding: the
migration requirements embed an explicit numbered block of seven core rules plus
seven transformation rules, and those fourteen govern this work in full, exactly
as an external rules document would. Reporting only the first fact would imply
that enterprise best practice is the sole standard here, which is wrong because
fourteen specific constraints apply; reporting only the second would misrepresent
where the rules came from. The requirements list the rules as numbered items
without names, so the identifiers above exist only so that a decision can be
traced back to the constraint that produced it. No rule has been invented and
none has been softened; enterprise best practice is applied on top of the
fourteen, never as a substitute for them.

R-7, BASELINE BEHAVIOUR IS THE TIE-BREAKER -- the rule that creates this capture.
Quoted with its substitution disclosed rather than made silently:

    "The application's observed behavior at the base commit on JDK 8 is the
    tie-breaker for any ambiguity, and each resolution must be documented."

    Editorial note: the rule's own text names the older runtime with a phrase
    this documentation tree's wording gate forbids. The substitution changes no
    meaning and is disclosed here rather than applied quietly.

This artefact is what makes the "on JDK 8, at the base commit" half of R-7
verifiable rather than merely asserted. That is why the runtime designation and
the base commit are both recorded above, and why the capture is irreversible:
nothing done later can reconstruct the runtime a measurement was taken on, which
is why baseline capture is the first executable action of the migration rather
than a validation afterthought. A digest or a test report without a recorded
runtime is an unlabelled measurement.

R-T7, EVIDENCE OVER EXIT CODES. Quoted verbatim:

    "Validation asserts on produced artifacts and captured output, never on
    process exit status alone. This is mandatory rather than stylistic because
    Gruntfile.js sets grunt.option('force', true), which masks task failures and
    lets a broken build exit zero."

Applied here: every probe above records the tool's own output, not merely that it
exited zero. Each command is captured with its error stream merged into its
output stream, because a version banner may be written to either. A probe whose
tool is absent is recorded as ABSENT with a deterministic, path-free record; it
is never silently omitted, and no version is ever inferred, guessed or copied
from documentation.

R-2 AND R-T3 ARE PARAPHRASED HERE, NEVER QUOTED, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. The text
of each names a module-access JVM argument literally, and this documentation tree
is subject to a recursive audit that requires zero such literals, so quoting
either rule verbatim would itself introduce the token the audit forbids.

    R-2 requires that production launch configuration not depend on JDK internal
    access -- that is, on a module-access JVM argument that opens or exports an
    otherwise-encapsulated JDK package to the unnamed module -- except where a
    pinned third-party dependency documentedly requires it, and that every such
    exception be documented. Observed: the production launch configuration
    declares no such argument, so the JDK access exceptions register is delivered
    empty -- empty because every measured requirement was removed at its source by
    advancing the dependency that needed it, not because none was looked for. That
    register is referred to here by title only, because its filename embeds the
    very token the audit forbids.

    R-T3 requires that a dependency failing under strong encapsulation be
    upgraded or replaced rather than accommodated by opening a JDK package.
    Observed across this migration, and itemised in that register: every
    strong-encapsulation failure was resolved the way R-T3 prescribes rather than
    by relaxing the platform -- two inside test libraries, three inside pinned
    production dependencies, and one compile-time call site in the application's
    own source. The application's own reflective code targets only application
    classes, and no security manager is installed anywhere. Production launch
    configuration therefore needs no exception at all.

R-1, justified changes, acting here as a scope fence: a change without a reason is
out of scope. No tool was installed to produce this capture -- the producer and
the renderer that laid out this artefact use only the POSIX toolset -- and no
field or section exists beyond the four contracted probes, the producer's own
emissions, the substitutions disclosure and this section.

R-4, genuine Node 20 execution. npm is the incoming package manager, which is why
PROBE 4 captures its version; under R-T5 that version matters beyond provenance,
because it governs the lockfile format the migrated side produces, so it is
recorded exactly. The pre-migration package manager is named nowhere in this
artefact, and nothing here presents it as a prerequisite or a recommendation.
R-4 also constrains overreach: the retained build pipeline was verified to
install and execute on Node 20, so the migrated replay runs the same unchanged
task graph and no build-tool change is implied.

R-5, no disabling of failing tests, with exclusions limited to failures already
present at baseline. This artefact is the label on the archived unit-test
evidence that the baseline-failure register cites row by row: an exclusion is
auditable only if the runtime under which those failures were observed is
recorded. The operational parallel is the absence rule stated above -- no probe
may be silently omitted.

R-6, document discovered defects rather than fixing them. Nothing was repaired to
make this capture look complete: no absent tool was installed, no banner was
fabricated and no anomaly was smoothed over. The migration's escape clause is
invoked exactly twice, and neither invocation is in this folder.

R-T1, namespace invariance. Nothing in this capture references the successor
namespace, a newer framework generation, a typed JavaScript dialect or a module
bundler. All are excluded from this migration and none is happening.

R-T2 and R-3, a single compile source of truth with no release-8 escape hatch.
Recorded as observed provenance of the tree this capture labels: at the base
commit the compiler contract is declared in exactly one of the 145 POMs, at
pom.xml:21, and consumed at six sites -- pom.xml:332-334 in the default compiler
plugin configuration and pom.xml:349-351 inside the log4j-plugin-processor
execution. That is the pre-migration state this baseline documents. It is not an
endorsement of that target for the migrated build, which compiles at release 17
from a single authoritative property.

R-T4, explicit pinning. Every version recorded above is an exact value read from
the tool itself. None is expressed as a range, as an approximation or as
"latest".

R-T6 is not engaged by this artefact: no dependency key, no install topology and
no output artifact name is touched here.

MIRROR OBLIGATION. The two sides of this capture use the identical filename, the
identical directory name, the identical command set in the identical order and
the identical field layout, so that a recursive diff between them shows the
intended runtime delta and nothing structural. No wall-clock time, host name,
user name, process identifier, random value or absolute path is recorded
anywhere above, because each would differ between two runs for reasons unrelated
to the runtime and would turn that comparison into noise.
